name: Many-Source and All-Pairs Shortest Distances
problem_statement: Compute a matrix of minimum path-weight sums for selected origins and destinations, including all-pairs queries.

normalization: Preserve all declared vertices, including isolated vertices.
Preserve direction; an undirected projection must be explicitly requested.
Declare the treatment of self-loops and parallel edges before execution; an adapter must reject unsupported cases.

problem_inputs.name: weight_mode
problem_inputs.description: Use unit distances or nonnegative weights.

required_outputs.name: distance_matrix
required_outputs.description: Rows and columns identify origins and destinations; unreachable pairs have null distance.

required_outputs.name: complete
required_outputs.description: Whether every requested pair was evaluated.

solution_semantics.objective: Compute the shortest distance for each requested pair.
solution_semantics.exactness: Exact within numeric tolerance. Batched SSSP and matrix-based implementations must return the same distances.
solution_semantics.duplicate_policy: Output identities refer to the normalized input; any multiplicities must follow the declared task.
solution_semantics.ordering: No output order or choice among equally valid optima is required unless specified by an input.

validation_rules: Compare against repeated CPU Dijkstra or Floyd-Warshall.
Diagonal entries for identical origin and destination are zero.
edge_cases: Empty origin/destination sets produce an empty matrix.
All-pairs output can require quadratic storage.

correctness: Compare against repeated CPU Dijkstra or Floyd-Warshall.
Diagonal entries for identical origin and destination are zero.
